August 24, 2026

The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, N.E.
Washington, D.C. 20426

Re:    Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Docket No. ER26-____-000
       Submission of Tariff Revisions to Modify the Conditional High Impact Large
       Load Policy to Accommodate Planned Outages

Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C. § 824d,
and Section 35.13 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”)
Regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. ("SPP"), as authorized by
its independent Board of Directors, submits revisions to the Open Access Transmission
Tariff (“Tariff”)1 to modify the Conditional High Impact Large Load (“CHILL”) policy
to accommodate planned Outages.

        SPP is requesting that the Commission issue an order in this docket as soon as
practicable, but not later than November 24, 2026, which is approximately 90 days after
submission of this filing. SPP requests an effective date of “12/31/9998”2 for the Tariff
Records submitted in this filing in order to allow SPP staff to develop, test, and move
the proposed revisions into the production phase of SPP’s software systems. SPP will
submit a filing with the Commission specifying a precise effective date prior to
implementation. SPP will work as quickly as practicable to technologically implement
the Tariff revisions proposed herein. As of the date of this filing, implementation is
targeted for the second quarter of 2027.

        SPP respectfully requests waiver of the Commission’s timing requirements to
allow these tariff revisions to be effective more than 120 days after the date of filing.

1

I.     STAKEHOLDER APPROVAL

2026;4 Regional Tariff Working Group ("RTWG") on June 25, 2026;5 and Markets and
Operations Policy Committee (“MOPC”) on July 14-15, 2026.6 While SPP recognizes
that stakeholder approval does not by itself cause a filing to be just and reasonable, SPP

II.    BACKGROUND, PURPOSE, AND JUSTIFICATION FOR PROPOSED
       TARIFF REVISIONS

       A. Background

       As noted in previous filings, SPP’s Regional Transmission Organization
(“RTO”) is experiencing a surge in requests to rapidly interconnect large loads to the
transmission system. In response, SPP has moved to adapt its processes to meet the
challenges to reliability and economic operation of its systems and to speed the
interconnection and operation of these large loads.

         SPP’s first filing added study processes for High Impact Large Loads (“HILL”)
and a High Impact Large Load Generation Assessment (“HILLGA”).8 The HILLGA
process, outlined in Attachment BB, facilitates the prompt interconnection of
generating resources that are specifically identified for and limited to serving a HILL,
at the request of the HILLGA Customer.9 SPP studies HILLGA Requests outside of its
existing generator interconnection process on a serial basis, but solely for the impact of

        With its next filing, SPP added Conditional High Impact Large Loads
(“CHILL”) and Conditional High Impact Large Load Service (“CHILLS”) to the
Tariff.16 The CHILLS Filing was a response to the challenge to provide transmission
service to these large loads. In the absence of CHILLS, the Tariff requires Transmission
Customers that desire firm transmission service to support new load additions to have
sufficient existing Designated Resources to serve both their existing load plus the new
load addition.17 CHILLS helps mitigate the challenges of integrating HILLs into the
Transmission System. With CHILLS, Transmission Customers are required to have
sufficient generation in-service prior to receiving CHILLS.18

        The CHILLS requirement to have sufficient generation mitigates affordability
concerns19 as increased generation supply should alleviate the price impacts from the
increase in demand from new large loads. This requirement also supports reliability by
requiring that adequate Resource capacity be interconnected to the Transmission
System.

        SPP requires CHILLs to choose a participation option, as defined in Attachment
AE, Section 2.22.1(c) or (d), so that SPP knows if the CHILL is to be supported by
specific Resources.20 This will enable SPP to properly study the requests for CHILLS
and to correctly apply operational checks on the CHILL. The first participation option
(“Option 1 CHILLS”) requires the Transmission Customer to have sufficient
Designated Resource capacity to serve its existing Network Load plus all of its existing
and proposed CHILLs. Under this option, there are no specific Resources supporting
the CHILL. The second participation option (“Option 2 CHILLS”) requires the

Transmission Customer to have generation capacity with an accreditation MW value,
as determined pursuant to Attachment AA of the Tariff, sufficient to cover the entire
CHILL. Option 2 capacity may have LLRIS or other interconnection service or be
Behind-The-Meter Generation.

        One of the requirements for Option 2 CHILLS is that its supporting Resource(s)
must be available for commitment and dispatch by the market. This availability is
determined by whether the Resource Offer is sufficient to meet the forecasted
withdrawals by the CHILL.21 Option 2 CHILLS does not require the Market Participant
to continuously run supporting generation, but it must be available, and the CHILL may
be curtailed to a zero net impact during emergencies.22 This sufficiency examination
will occur when SPP considers unit commitment23 and is not limited to the MW offered,
but can consider other Offer24 parameters. The original CHILLS Filing did not include
any exception to this requirement for Outages.

       B. SPP’s Proposed Tariff Changes

        With the present filing, SPP proposes a limited exception to the generation
sufficiency check for Option 2 CHILLS. This exception is narrowly tailored to mitigate
both the reliability and economic concerns that led to the generation sufficiency
requirement for CHILLS. SPP’s proposed changes only apply to Option 2 CHILLs, as
Option 1 CHILLs are not supported by specific Resources.

       The first part of SPP’s proposed Tariff changes defines the circumstances for
allowing planned Outages. Currently, under Attachment AE, Section 2.22.1(d), the
CHILL can be curtailed “when the sum of the available capacity for the supporting
resources is less than the CHILL.”25 SPP’s current Tariff revisions would relax this

requirement when the Resource is taking a Scheduled Resource Outage26 submitted at
least 14 Calendar Days in advance of the planned start time.27 Market Participants may
not remove the Resource from service unless SPP approves it.28 If the Resource takes
an Outage anyway, it will still be subject to the sufficiency examination. This limitation
keeps the exception for supporting Resources narrow, thereby limiting impacts to both
reliability and economics.

        SPP proposes to allow the CHILL to stay online during Scheduled Resource
Outages,29 subject to all other CHILL curtailment protocols. This is essentially
conditional approval to stay online. CHILLs with multiple supporting Resources that
can serve at least the CHILL minus the accredited MW of the Resource(s) on Outage
may still operate as normal regardless of Outage status since they can pass the
sufficiency examination.

         Although having a supporting Resource on an Outage that meets the
requirements exempts that portion of the CHILL MW from the sufficiency check, it is
still subject to the other conditions that can result in CHILL curtailments.30 Essentially,
coverage of the CHILL MW for the supporting Resource on an approved Scheduled
Resource Outage will be treated like Option 1 CHILLS.

       For example, assume that a CHILL is 100 MW and is supported by two 100
MW Resources, with the first a wind Resource at 20% accreditation and the second a
gas Resource at 80% accreditation. If the gas Resource is on an Outage, it will pass the
CHILL Resource sufficiency check if the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating
Limit of the wind Resource is greater than or equal to the CHILL (100 MW) minus the
accredited MW of the gas Resource (80 MW). If the wind Resource passes this check

(at least 20 MW), the portion of the CHILL not covered by the wind Resource (80 MW)
is considered like CHILL Option 1 MW, and may be served by the market. If the wind
Resource does not pass the minimal check, then the CHILL will be curtailed.31 This
policy incentivizes the availability of supporting Resources not on Outage, provides
the CHILL a pathway to avoid potentially being curtailed through similar treatment to
an Option 1 CHILL if its other Resources are sufficiently available, and mitigates
potential economic and reliability impacts to the market.

         These changes are just and reasonable as they improve the usability of CHILLS
by allowing the supporting Resource a path to take Outages to maintain their equipment
without necessarily curtailing the load under circumstances that mitigate the impact to
reliability and mitigate the economic effects on other loads. This necessary
maintenance can help lead to improved performance and readiness when not on Outage.
SPP’s proposal keeps the ability to curtail CHILLs during periods where it could impact
reliability.32

        To further support reliability, SPP proposes to incentivize supporting
generation availability during Emergency Conditions. SPP proposes to revise
Attachment U to allow Option 2 CHILLS supporting generation to receive
compensation for qualified planned Outages deferred during system emergencies when
the Resource is made available, but not for deferment for other reasons.33 This is the
same compensation offered for other generators on approved Outages. This change is
just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory since these Resources will be on an
approved Outage that is rescheduled at the request of SPP to make the Resource
available in Emergency Conditions. That means that the Resource is sufficiently
similarly situated to other Resources in similar circumstances where similar
compensation is warranted.

III.   DESCRIPTION OF TARIFF REVISIONS

       A.     Attachment U Section B (Compensation for Generator Owners)

       SPP proposes to add a new paragraph to Section B of Attachment U as follows:

              Scheduled Resource Outages for supporting Resources for a
              Conditional High Impact Large Load (CHILL) participating under
              Section 2.22.1(d) of Attachment AE of this Tariff are solely Qualified
              if, in addition to the criteria in this Section B, the Outage is rescheduled
              at the request of the Transmission Provider to make the Resource
              available in Emergency Conditions as described in Section 2.22.2(2)(b)
              of Attachment AE of this Tariff and the Resource was made available
              as described in Section 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of
              Attachment AE of this Tariff.34

       B.     Attachment AE Section 2.22.1 (Conditional High Impact Large
              Load)

       SPP proposes revisions to Section 2.22.1(d) of Attachment AE as follows:

              (d)     If the Transmission Customer has executed the service
                      agreement pursuant to Addendum 1 to Attachment BA of the
                      Tariff and, instead of having sufficient Designated Resources
                      capacity to serve existing Network Load plus the CHILL
                      existing and proposed CHILLs, the Transmission Customer has
                      sufficient generation capacity with an accreditation MW value,
                      as determined pursuant to Attachment AA of the Tariff, that is
                      sufficient to cover the entire CHILL, the CHILL must agree to

                      AE, (2) due to transmission limitations, (3) due to a Local
                      Reliability Issue, (4) due to an unfavorable net impact to the
                      transmission system during system CHILL Curtailments, or (5)
                      due to Emergency Conditions. The CHILL and supporting
                      Resources must follow the requirements specified in the Market

IV.    EFFECTIVE DATE AND REQUEST FOR WAIVER

        SPP is requesting an effective date of “12/31/9998” for the Tariff Records
included with this filing. The expected effective date of the Tariff revisions included
herein is currently in the second quarter of 2027, which is more than 90 days after
filing. Therefore, SPP requests waiver of the Commission’s notice requirements.37
Good cause exists for the proposed revisions to be effective in the second quarter of
2027 in accordance with the Commission’s waiver of notice requirement codified in
Section 35.11 of the Commission’s regulations38 because SPP will need a number of
months to develop, test, and implement the software system changes for the Tariff
revisions proposed herein. SPP requests the Commission issue an order by November
24, 2026, to allow SPP sufficient time to make the necessary software changes prior to
implementation.

B.     Compensation to Generator Owners

       Owners of generating units within the SPP Region and owners of generating units
pseudo-tied into one of the SPP Balancing Authority Areas shall coordinate the scheduling of
Scheduled Resource Outages for the maintenance of generating units with the Transmission
Provider. The Transmission Provider shall review the Scheduled Resource Outage requests
submitted by Generator Owners. Any Generator Owner that reschedules a Qualified Scheduled
Resource Outage at the direction of the Transmission Provider or the SPP Reliability
Coordinator is eligible to be reimbursed by the Transmission Provider for incremental costs
incurred, in accordance with Good Utility Practice, as a direct result of any such rescheduling.
Generator Owners shall use best efforts to minimize incremental costs resulting from a
rescheduled Scheduled Resource Outage.
       Criteria described herein must be met in order to consider the Scheduled Resource
Outage Qualified for the purposes of Attachment U cost recovery. To be considered Qualified,
the Scheduled Resource Outage for a generating unit within the SPP Region or a generating unit
pseudo-tied into an SPP Balancing Authority Area must be submitted to the Transmission
Provider at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the start of the scheduled maintenance. The
Transmission Provider then has fourteen (14) calendar days from the submission date to respond
to the Scheduled Resource Outage request. If the Transmission Provider denies the Scheduled
Resource Outage within the fourteen (14) calendar day response window, then the Scheduled
Resource Outage is not considered Qualified. Scheduled Resource Outage requests not acted
upon by the Transmission Provider within the fourteen (14) calendar day response window will
be considered Qualified. For Scheduled Resource Outage requests submitted more than three
hundred sixty-five (365) calendar days in advance, the Transmission Provider’s fourteen (14)
calendar day response window will start three hundred sixty-five (365) calendar days prior to the
requested start date of the Scheduled Resource Outage. Modification requests to a Qualified
Scheduled Resource Outage will not alter the Qualified status of the Scheduled Resource Outage.
If the Transmission Provider accepts a modification to a Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage,
the modified Scheduled Resource Outage remains Qualified. If the Transmission Provider denies
a modification to a Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage, then the existing Scheduled Resource
Outage remains unchanged and maintains Qualified status.
           Scheduled Resource Outages for supporting Resources for a Conditional High Impact
Large Load (CHILL) participating under Section 2.22.1(d) of Attachment AE of this Tariff are
solely Qualified if, in addition to the criteria in this Section B, the Outage is rescheduled at the
request of the Transmission Provider to make the Resource available in Emergency Conditions
as described in Section 2.22.2(2)(b) of Attachment AE of this Tariff and the Resource was made
available as described in Section 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of Attachment AE of this
Tariff.
          All incremental costs for which compensation is sought or provided under this Section B
are to be fully documented by the Generator Owner, supported by information such as invoices,
receipts or contracts, and such documentation shall be made available to the Transmission
Provider. The Generator Owner shall provide the Transmission Provider with an attestation as to
the prudence and validity of all incremental costs for which compensation is requested as well as
information that the Transmission Provider determines is necessary to substantiate the
incremental costs of rescheduling a Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage. The Generator Owner
shall forward to the Transmission Provider: (1) the initial statement and supporting
documentation of the total incremental cost of rescheduling a Qualified Scheduled Resource
Outage within forty-five (45) calendar days of the end of the time period of the rescheduled
Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage; and (2) the final statement of such total incremental cost,
accompanied by any additional documentation and the required attestation, within ninety (90)
calendar days of the end of the time period of the rescheduled Qualified Scheduled Resource
Outage. Section D of this Attachment U describes the manner in which the Transmission
Provider is to recover the costs of all reimbursements of incremental costs made to the Generator
Owner pursuant to this Section B.
          The following are the incremental costs resulting from a rescheduled Qualified Scheduled
Resource Outage that are eligible for recovery by the Generator Owner:
          (1)    Incremental labor costs: The labor costs eligible for recovery from the
                 Transmission Provider shall be the actual out-of-pocket incremental labor costs
                 incurred by the Generator Owner only because of the rescheduling of the
                 Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage. Incremental overhead costs associated
                 with this labor also can be recovered if substantiating documentation is provided
                 of such expenditures.
 (2)   Incremental materials costs: The materials costs eligible for recovery from the
      Transmission Provider shall be the actual out-of-pocket incremental materials
      costs incurred by the Generator Owner only because of the rescheduling of the
      Qualified Scheduled Resource Outage.
 2.22.1 Conditional High Impact Large Load

(a)   A Conditional High Impact Large Load (CHILL) is the portion of a HILL that is eligible
      to connect to the Transmission System and receive CHILLS as described in Attachment
      BA and Part VII of this Tariff. A CHILL must follow all requirements listed for HILL in
      Section 2.22 of this Attachment AE, as well as provide the additional requirements listed
      in their Conditional High Impact Large Load Service Agreement (CHILLSA).


(b)   Additionally, Conditional High Impact Large Loads must:
      1.     Submit separate Real-Time telemetry for each CHILL in accordance with the
             Market Protocols;
      2.     Submit separate bill meter values in accordance with Section 2.5 of this
             Attachment AE for each CHILL;
      3.     Not register as a Demand Response Resource;
      4.     Not be a Demand Response Load;
      5.     Not be Critical Load.
      6.     Choose a participation option as defined by Sections 2.22.1(c) or 2.22.1(d); and
      7.     Reflect any caps or limits in the CHILL’s nonconforming load forecast. Failure to
             do so may result in Curtailment of the CHILL.


(c)   If the Transmission Customer has executed the service agreement pursuant to Addendum
      1 to Attachment BA of the Tariff and the Transmission Customer has sufficient
      Designated Resource capacity to serve existing Network Load plus the CHILL existing
      and proposed CHILLs, the CHILL must agree to be curtailable in the event of (1)
      transmission limitations, (2) system CHILL Curtailments (3) under Emergency
      Conditions, or (4) a Local Reliability Issue.


(d)   If the Transmission Customer has executed the service agreement pursuant to Addendum
      1 to Attachment BA of the Tariff and, instead of having sufficient Designated Resources
      capacity to serve existing Network Load plus the CHILL existing and proposed CHILLs,
      the Transmission Customer has sufficient generation capacity with an accreditation MW
       value, as determined pursuant to Attachment AA of the Tariff, that is sufficient to cover
      the entire CHILL, the CHILL must agree to be curtailable: (1) when the sum of the
      available capacity for the supporting Resources is less than the CHILL unless one or
      more of the supporting Resources is on a Scheduled Resource Outage submitted at least
      14 Calendar Days in advance of the planned start time as described in Section
      2.22.2(1)(c) of this Attachment AE, (2) due to transmission limitations, (3) due to a Local
      Reliability Issue, (4) due to an unfavorable net impact to the transmission system during
      system CHILL Curtailments, or (5) due to Emergency Conditions. The CHILL and
      supporting Resources must follow the requirements specified in the Market Protocols in
      order for the supporting Resource to be considered available capacity for supporting the
      CHILL.


(e)   A CHILL must respond to all Curtailment instructions, initiate Curtailment within the
      amount of time specified in the Market Protocols, and ramp down to the instructed
      amount at a rate as outlined in the Market Protocols, unless otherwise directed by the SPP
      Balancing Authority, Reliability Coordinator, or local transmission operator. A CHILL
      may be disconnected from the Transmission System by the transmission operator at any
      time.
 2.22.2 Resources Supporting a HILL or CHILL

(1)    The following applies to Resources supporting a CHILL participating under Section
2.22.1(d) of this Attachment AE:
       (a)    Resources supporting a CHILL must submit Resource Offers sufficient to cover
              forecasted withdrawals by the CHILL as described in the Market Protocols.
       (b)    When a Resource supports more than one CHILL, the Resource must be split, and
              it must be registered such that there are the same number of registered Resources
              as the number of CHILLs the facility is supporting.
       (c)    Resources supporting a CHILL may take a Scheduled Resource Outage scheduled
              at least 14 Calendar Days in advance of the planned start time and the CHILL will
              not be curtailed solely due to supporting Resource insufficiency as described in
              Section 2.22.1(d)(1) of this Attachment AE when:
              (i)    There is one supporting Resource for the CHILL and the Resource is on a
                     Scheduled Resource Outage.
              (ii)   There are multiple supporting Resources for the CHILL, and the sum of
                     the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits for the available
                     supporting Resources is greater than or equal to the capacity needed to
                     support the CHILL minus the accredited MW of the Resource(s) on the
                     Scheduled Resource Outage, subject to the requirements in Section
                     2.22.2(2)(b) and the Market Protocols.
(2)    Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service as defined in Attachment
       BB of the Tariff must:
       (a)    Follow all rules and restrictions included in their HILLGIA.
       (b)    Ensure the sum of the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of
              supporting Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, as
              defined in Attachment BB of the Tariff, does not exceed the submitted HILL or
              CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL except when
              directed by the Transmission Provider to mitigate Emergency Conditions or as
              specified in the Resource’s generator interconnection agreement.
 (3)   Behind-The-Meter Generation supporting a HILL, including any portion of a HILL which
      is a CHILL, and registered in the Integrated Marketplace must abide by the following
      rules:
      (a)      The load Meter Settlement Location associated with the Behind-The-Meter
               Generation must not have an injection into the Transmission System without
               appropriate transmission service;
      (b)      Submit a Day-Ahead and Real Time Balancing Market Offer where the Resource
               Maximum Normal, Economic, Regulation and Emergency Capacity Operating
               limit must not exceed the projected demand at that load Meter Settlement
               Location for an Operating Hour or Dispatch Interval, unless the Resource has
               appropriate transmission service.
